JOINING STAFF WITH
CAMPUS CRUSADE
To picture the structure of the Campus Ministry, it is
helpful to imagine a multi-lane highway. The scope of
our mission is so large we have segmented the Campus
Ministry into separate, specialized, initiatives. We call
them lanes.
vibrant athletic programs, dynamic school spirit, or
rich histories, these campuses radiate excitement and
embody the academic ideal.
There is the lane that focuses on planting new
ministries, Catalytic. Our focused outreach to ethnic
students is the ESM (Ethnic Student Ministry) lane.
Our traditional, and foundational ministries are the
Staffed Campus lane. Efforts to establish campus
ministries around the world are accomplished through
our WSN (Worldwide Student Network) lane. And our
support lanes, some call them the yellow lines between
the lanes, are Human Resources, Operations and Fund
Development. Staff in these lanes provide service
for everything from graphics and web technology to
funding and staff placement. Here you’ll find a basic
overview of each of these lanes.
From these schools come some of the sharpest
thinkers; including faculty and students who lead in
their fields of business, medicine, law, education, and
politics. Through evangelism and discipleship you’ll
be daily investing in the lives of students and offering
a personal encounter with Jesus Christ, which will
ultimately contribute to the spread of movements of
believers everywhere.
Picture leading a small group Bible study in a freshman
residence hall and engaging in a lively discussion with
a junior about ways to take the gospel to all corners
of their university; including students in theater,
engineering, or on foreign exchange. Imagine your
role of helping leaders launch movements in dozens
of communities within their campus where active
ministries have never existed.
Catalytic
In metro areas, catalytic teams are reaching students
on 20 – 30 campuses in their city. Other teams are
pioneering ministries on unreached campuses. You
would help students, volunteers, and churches learn
how to effectively develop “win, build, and send”
movements that can reach every student with the
gospel.
Consider offering students an experience that will
expand their view of God’s work in the world and how
they can be used in the Great Commission. Perhaps
this means inviting them to a fall or winter conference,
or stateside and international summer project, which
God may use to develop them profoundly. Coach a
student on how to lead a spring break outreach or
teach them to study God’s Word in such a way that they
will also disciple others for a lifetime.
Staff Campuses
Imagine working with a team of five to ten other staff
committed to building spiritual movements within
a traditional campus environment. These campuses
are places like The University of Colorado, Texas
A&M, UCLA, The University of Michigan, Purdue,
and more. Campuses are typically larger, localized,
and comprised of a multitude of micro communities.

EPIC. Epic is a ministry of Campus Crusade for Christ
which was designed to reach a people group that is
often overlooked – the Asian American people. Asians
are the fastest growing ethnic group in America whose
numbers have grown by fifty percent since 1990. Epic
has been strategically mobilized as a campus ministry
in order to transform college students into Christ-
centered laborers who will give back to the community
and the world. Learn more about Epic at www.
epicmovement.com
SALARY
It is the policy of Campus Crusade for Christ
International that each staff member develops a team
of ministry partners to support his/her ministry.
Campus Crusade’s salary structure is based on need,
not on a position of leadership. All staff members,
including the president, Steve Douglass, work under
the same financial policies and pay scale. In order to
keep our staff free from financial distractions and
focused on our mission, our salary structure promotes
a moderate lifestyle, longevity in ministry, and
individual freedom and responsibility for staff.
Each staff member starts with a base salary which
is then increased based on age, the size of family,
geographic location, and tenure to arrive at a
maximum salary. Staff members may then request
their salary to be any amount between the minimum
required salary and the maximum amount. Additional
salary may be requested for special needs like the
purchase of a car or college tuition for children.
Destino. Destino is a ministry of Campus Crusade for
Christ directed toward the Hispanic community in
the United States. God is working on your campus. We
are committed to helping emerging leaders grow in
their relationship with God and empowering students
to take the truth of Jesus Christ to the campus, to
the community, and to the world. Learn more about
Destino at www.destinomovement.com

Group Life Insurance
A generous basic life insurance program is offered for
staff members at various stages of life. Our basic life
insurance provides $50,000 for singles, $100,000 each
for couples without dependents, and $250,000 each
for couples with dependents.
Disability Income & Workmen’s Compensation
Campus Crusade also provides Long-Term Disability
and Worker’s Compensation in the event of a job-
related injury.
Vacation / Holidays:
Each staff member receives two weeks of vacation
a year once they report to their ministry location.
Additional weeks of vacation are also added with
tenure. The organization recognizes eight paid
holidays per year.

Here you’ll find the basic overview of the application

forms, it is anything but impersonal. Some of the finest

to your growth and development. A small team of
Sending Associates will be intimately familiar with the
specifics of your application and will work diligently
to make an acceptance decision and offer feedback
tailored specifically to where you are in your journey
with the Lord.

If you’ve served as a US Campus Intern, you’ll probably

completed a STINT or Internship within the last 12

APPLICATION TIMELINE
Step 1: Complete and submit Online Application
Step 2: Complete any additional application
materials as directed by the Sending &
Recruiting Team.
Step 3: We will schedule a Staff Interview in
your area if you haven’t already had one at a CCC
conference.
Step 4: All Application materials must be
received by April 1 for Summer training and
November 1 for Winter training.
Step 5: You will be called for a phone interview to
follow up on information received in both your
initial interview and application.
Step 6: Once approved, you will receive a Pre-
Acceptance decision within 6-8 weeks from the
date that we received your completed application
materials.
Step 7: If you receive a Pre-Acceptance to staff, a
Background Check will be performed.
Step 8: Upon completion of the Background
Check, you will receive your Final Acceptance
decision.
Step 9: We will send you information on New
Staff Training, Ministry Partner Development,
and your staff account number.
Step 10: Attend New Staff Training. (Held in
January/February and June/July.)
For more information on joining staff with Campus
Crusade go to the Campus Ministry Website.
